title: Ordinary finite-coefficient affine-line unit over a Noetherian base
statement: Let $B$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], meaning that $B$ admits a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. Let $\ell$ be a prime invertible on $B$, let $n\geq1$, and put $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Let $p:\mathbf A^1_B\to B$ be the projection [def-sbc-affine-space]. In the ordinary small-etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with inverse image and direct image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact, def-weil-pbc-direct-image], the canonical adjunction unit $\Lambda_B\longrightarrow Rp_*\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_B}$ is an isomorphism. Neither regularity nor a structure morphism from $B$ to a field is assumed.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 1.5, proof on printed page 227: homotopy invariance for schemes over Z[1/m], specialized to the one-dimensional affine-space projection and m = ell^n.

proof.text: Put $m=\ell^n$ and $P=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};B)$, with projection $q$. The standard charts [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] are $D(x_0)=\operatorname{Spec}R[t]$ and $D(x_1)=\operatorname{Spec}R[s]$ over each $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset B$, with $s=t^{-1}$ on the intersection. The closed locus $x_0=0$ is empty in the first chart and is $s=0$ in the second; these equations agree on the overlap and identify this closed subscheme with $B$. Write $i:B\hookrightarrow P$ for it. Its complementary open $j:U\hookrightarrow P$ is $D(x_0)=\mathbf A^1_B$, with $qj=p$ and $qi=\operatorname{id}_B$. By [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], $q$ is proper, hence of finite type; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $P$ Noetherian. Thus all Noetherian hypotheses of the proper projection formula below hold, without requiring $B$ to be regular or over a field.

source.place: Tags 01ND, 01NG: the two projective-line charts; Morphisms Tag 01T6 for the Noetherian hypothesis.

proof.text: Use [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] with $A=\Lambda$ and $m=\ell^n$. Set $T_B=\Lambda_B(1)[2]$, $T_P=\Lambda_P(1)[2]=q^{-1}T_B$, and $K=\Lambda_B(-1)[-2]$. Evaluation gives $K\otimes^L T_B\cong\Lambda_B$ and $q^{-1}K\otimes^L T_P\cong\Lambda_P$: the finite Tate line is locally free of rank one, so its dual evaluations are isomorphisms, and the shifts cancel. Write $F=Rq_*$ and $G(L)=q^{-1}L\otimes^L T_P$. The entire ordinary-etale adjunction $F\dashv G$ and the decomposition $b:T_B\oplus\Lambda_B\xrightarrow{\sim}FT_P$ are [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction]. Its trace is $t=\operatorname{pr}_2b^{-1}$ and its actual counit at $L$ is $(1_L\otimes t)\pi_{L,T_P}^{-1}$. Here $\pi$ is the canonical proper projection isomorphism [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection]. In particular $GK\cong\Lambda_P$.

source.place: Full projective-line adjunction, together with its normalized decomposition; specialize the coefficient ring to Z/ell^n and the input to Lambda(-1)[-2].

proof.text:
Tensor $b$ with $K$ and use the same canonical projection isomorphism to obtain
$$d:\Lambda_B\oplus K=(K\otimes^L T_B)\oplus K\xrightarrow{1_K\otimes b}K\otimes^L FT_P\xrightarrow{\pi_{K,T_P}}F\Lambda_P.$$
Its first component is the ordinary $q^{-1}\dashv F$ unit $\eta_q:\Lambda_B\to F\Lambda_P$. Indeed the first component of $b$ is the unit at $T_B$. The map $\pi$ of [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] is $Rq_*(\sigma)\,\mathrm{PF}_q\,\sigma$, where $\mathrm{PF}_q$ is by definition the morphism adjoint to $(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{ord}}\otimes1)$ composed with the inverse-image tensor comparison [def-kun-projection-formula-map] (the same adjoint-of-counit construction as [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]); the symmetries $\sigma$ commute with the units by naturality. By this adjoint-of-counit description of $\pi$, the transpose of the first component of $d$ is $1_{q^{-1}K}$ tensored with $\varepsilon^{\mathrm{ord}}_{T_P}\,q^{-1}(\eta_{q,T_B})$, followed by evaluation. This is the identity of $\Lambda_P$ by the ordinary triangle identity. The counit $\epsilon_K:FGK=F\Lambda_P\to K$ of the different adjunction $F\dashv G$ satisfies $\epsilon_Kd=\operatorname{pr}_2$, since its formula in Step 2 cancels $\pi$ and $t b=\operatorname{pr}_2$. Thus both the unit and trace have specified coordinates.

source.place: Tags 07A6 and 0B56: derived adjunction and the adjoint-of-counit projection map; elementary substitution of the two normalized maps from Step 2.

proof.text:
Let $i^!$ denote the ordinary right adjoint of $i_*$ provided by [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle], and write $c:i_*i^!\to\operatorname{id}$ for its counit. The termwise $i_*$ is exact [lem-per-etale-closed-sheaf-internal-adjunction], so it computes the derived direct image $Ri_*$. Since $qi=\operatorname{id}_B$, [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition](5) therefore identifies $Fi_*$ canonically with the identity. Composing $i_*\dashv i^!$ and $F\dashv G$ gives $Fi_*\dashv i^!G$, whose counit at $L$ is
$$Fi_*i^!GL\xrightarrow{F(c_{GL})}FGL\xrightarrow{\epsilon_L}L$$
by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Compare this with the identity adjunction by [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint]. It follows that this displayed counit, regarded as $i^!GL\to L$, is an isomorphism. Let $\theta:K\xrightarrow{\sim}i^!GK$ be its inverse at $K$. After $GK=\Lambda_P$, the map $f=F(c_{\Lambda_P})\,\theta:K\to F\Lambda_P$ therefore satisfies $\epsilon_K f=1_K$. This obtains the needed closed-support value from the two adjunctions, without an absolute-purity assertion about $B$.

source.place: Full projective-line adjunction and its counit; Stacks categories.tex Tag 0DV0 (lemma-compose-counits) and uniqueness of adjoints for the section at infinity.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] to $\Lambda_P$ and apply $F=Rq_*$. This preserves distinguished triangles by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. The direct-image composition comparison [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition](5) identifies the third term with $R(qj)_*\Lambda_U=Rp_*\Lambda_U$. Identify the first term with $K$ using $Fi_*=\operatorname{id}$ and $\theta$, and identify the middle term using $d$. We get a distinguished triangle
$$K\xrightarrow{u}\Lambda_B\oplus K\xrightarrow{v}C\xrightarrow{\partial}K[1],\qquad C=Rp_*\Lambda_U.$$
The second arrow before these identifications is $F$ of the ordinary open adjunction unit. By Steps 3 and 4, $\operatorname{pr}_2u=\epsilon_Kf=1_K$. Hence $u=(a,1_K)$, where $a=\operatorname{pr}_1d^{-1}f$. No identification of $a$ with a Chern class is needed.

source.place: Support triangle with its actual counit and open unit; Stacks etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0A45, lemma-cohomology-with-support-triangle.

proof.text:
Here is the split-triangle calculation with all arrows retained. By [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact](i), also on rotated triangles, $vu=0$ and $u[1]\partial=0$. Applying the left inverse $\operatorname{pr}_2[1]$ gives $\partial=0$. Put $z=\operatorname{pr}_1-a\operatorname{pr}_2:\Lambda_B\oplus K\to\Lambda_B$. Since $zu=0$, [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact](i) gives $w:C\to\Lambda_B$ with $wv=z$. Therefore $w(v\operatorname{in}_1)=1$. Also
$$((v\operatorname{in}_1)w-1_C)v=v(\operatorname{in}_1z-1)=-vu\operatorname{pr}_2=0.$$
Part (ii) of the same Hom-out exactness says this difference factors through $\partial$, so it is zero. Thus $v\operatorname{in}_1:\Lambda_B\to C$ is an isomorphism with inverse $w$.

It remains to identify the isomorphism, rather than just its endpoints. Step 3 identifies $d\operatorname{in}_1$ with $\eta_q$. Step 5 therefore identifies $v\operatorname{in}_1$ with $\Lambda_B\xrightarrow{\eta_q}Rq_*\Lambda_P\xrightarrow{Rq_*(\eta_j)}Rq_*Rj_*\Lambda_U$. Under the canonical composition comparison this is the unit for $p=qj$. More explicitly the ordinary inverse images are exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and the small-etale module-sheaf categories are Grothendieck abelian [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian], so [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] applies to $q^{-1},j^{-1},p^{-1}$ and their specified direct-image right adjoints. Its normalized derived comparison is the degreewise direct-image composition on injective representatives, and its unit is exactly $Rq_*(\eta_j)\eta_q$ by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Thus Step 6 proves that the canonical unit in the statement is invertible. All operations used are on ordinary small-etale module derived categories.

Then ε_K d = pr_2 and the first component of d is η_q (triangle identity). The composite counit of Fi_* ⊣ i^!G is invertible by uniqueness of right adjoints, so pr_2 u = 1. I redid the split-triangle algebra (∂=0, w(v in_1)=1, ((v in_1)w−1)v = −vu pr_2 = 0), and κ^D identifies the result with the canonical unit for p=qj.
